**Triage — graded.** `tests` · `priority:p3` · `pm:queue` · `domain:services`; `finding` removed. ⭐ **`finding` box now empty for this round.** Adopted as filed.

## Verified at `origin/main`

- ✅ The predicate is spelled as the card says: `approval-service.ts:5228` — `can_override: row.status === 'pending' && …`. So the flag really is the gate's own condition, and a pin is the only thing holding them together.
- ✅ The platform-admin case carries **both** assertions, with the exact comment the card quotes:
  - `approval-revise.test.ts:473` — `expect(seen!.viewer!.can_override).toBe(true);`
  - `:477` — `expect(out.resumed).toBe(true); // resumed down the reject branch`
- ✅ The sibling loop at `:439` runs `[['platform admin', PLATFORM_ADMIN, …], ['tenant admin', TENANT_ADMIN, …]]` and asserts `can_override … toBe(false)` at `:443` — confirming the card's central point exactly: **both** postures are pinned in the "no" direction, only one in the "yes" direction.
- ✅ The tenant-admin case at `:484` carries neither.
- ✅ `RECORD_LOCKED` is present (3 occurrences), so PR #14750 has landed. ⇒ No sequencing constraint; this is claimable now.

## The card's own mid-sentence correction is the right call

The filer wrote, then corrected in place: "such a regression would red the recall assertions. The gap that stays invisible is the narrower one: the **flag** going false while the **gate** stays permissive (or vice versa) for `organization_admin` on `pending`."

✅ That second statement is the accurate one, and it is what sets the priority. This is not an unguarded security gate — a regression in `isOverrideActor` for `organization_admin` would redden the existing recall assertions. What is unobserved is strictly the **agreement** between flag and gate for one posture in one status. Real drift risk, no live exposure. ⇒ `p3`.

I would rather see a correction left visible in a card than a tidy claim that overstates. It cost nothing here and it told me which half to weigh.

## Scope — terminal, two lines

Add to the existing tenant-admin case, mirroring the platform-admin idiom the file already uses at `:473`/`:477`: read the request as `TENANT_ADMIN` before the recall and assert `viewer.can_override === true`; assert `out.resumed` after it. Same file, same block, no new fixture.

⛔ **Do not touch the `APPROVALS_HOOK_PACKAGE` import at `:22`.** It is pre-existing on `main` and already frozen as TS6133 in `test-typecheck-debt.json` for this file. Clearing it moves a ledger, which is a different change class and a different review. If your editor or a lint autofix removes it, ⛔ put it back and note it in the report — a green diff that quietly shrinks a debt ledger is exactly the rider this card is fenced against.

⛔ Do not re-open the lock-release gap: #14602 is closed by PR #14750 and that work is done.

## Dedupe

✅ Accepted with its stated limit. Same note as on #14756: the `search_issues` zero-result the filer worked around is #14743, and the cause is GitHub qualifiers (`repo:`, `is:`, `label:`) placed inside `query`, where they are matched as text rather than parsed. Scope goes in the `owner`/`repo` **parameters** and `query` takes a natural-language sentence. The lane-listing fallback was the correct call, and flagging the weaker dedupe rather than hiding it is what made this gradeable without a re-check.

## PM ACCEPT — PR #14845, head `b51251903`. Verified against the tree, not the report.

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. R19. **Ruling of record — comments read: 1, and it IS the ruling: `issuecomment-5518661168`**, read in full before dispatch.

**Three-dot changeset: 1 file, 5 insertions.** Exactly the "terminal, two lines" scope.

⭐ **The dev caught a trap I would have wanted flagged**: `git diff origin/main --stat` showed **6 files**, because `origin/main` moved from its branch point `2d40f9146` to `f3ae441fa` under it while it worked. The real changeset is the three-dot / recorded-base diff, which I re-derived myself: **1 file, 5 insertions**. Reading the two-dot diff would have made this look like a scope violation.

## Both fences verified by me

| ruling's ⛔ | verified at head `b51251903` |
|---|---|
| do not touch the `APPROVALS_HOOK_PACKAGE` import at `:22` | present and untouched — `import { bindApprovalLockHook, APPROVALS_HOOK_PACKAGE } from './lifecycle-hooks.js';` |
| clearing it would move a debt ledger | `test-typecheck-debt.json` blob **`130e603a028540a348f4028bdefb7d173d634a0b`** — byte-identical at head and at `origin/main` |

⭐ The blob comparison is the right form of that check: the ruling's worry was "a green diff that quietly shrinks a debt ledger", and blob equality is the only thing that rules it out completely. The dev also ran `check:type-check-debt` repo-wide after building the closure — *"surplus: none — every entry sits exactly at its measurement"* — which is the same fence measured from the other side.

## ⭐ It declined to add a third assertion, and was right to

The platform-admin case carries a third line, `expect(seen!.status).toBe('pending')`. The dev deliberately did **not** mirror it, and said so in the PR body: the ruling's scope is terminal and names two assertions, `RECORD_LOCKED` on the line above already establishes the status, and an unnamed third is exactly the rider this card is fenced against.

That is the harder call — mirroring the sibling case *looks* like consistency. Declining, and putting the omission on the record rather than leaving it silent, is what the fence actually asked for.

## Ablation — three legs, and the honest one is the most useful

- **Leg C (load-bearing)** — surgical: `&& (context as any)?.posture !== TENANT_ADMIN` added to the `can_override` expression only. ⇒ `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed | 22 skipped (24)`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true` at `:487:42`. ⭐ **The platform-admin reverse check stayed GREEN in that same run** while the tenant-admin one went red — so the new assertion pins the tenant-admin posture *specifically*, and nothing else in the file already covered it. That comparison is what makes this evidence rather than a smoke test.
- **Leg B** — `resumed = true` → `false` on recall's non-revise-window path ⇒ red at `:491:27`.
- **Leg A**, kept and reported as observed rather than reshaped: dropping the `posture === TENANT_ADMIN` disjunct from `isOverrideActor` reddens the line but as a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`, because `isOverrideActor` doubles as `loadRequest`'s **read-visibility** predicate — so the request comes back `null` instead of a row with a false flag. ⭐ Reporting that as-is, then building leg C to isolate the flag, is exactly right; forcing leg A into the expected shape would have hidden a real property of the code.

Each leg: mutation proved on disk by removed-text count 0 / injected-text count 1 **plus** blob change off `8b10e70d…`; restore proved by blob equality back **and** empty `git diff HEAD`, with an empty hash treated as failure. ⛔ No comment marker.

## Clause ② — `no`

Test-only, 5 insertions, no production code. `skip-changeset` justified on the package's `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]` and `tsup` entry `src/index.ts` — nothing this PR touches is published. Applied additively and read back.

**Gates**: 29 families derived at the final commit (the script took its own changeset; "1 path"). 28 green. 1 NOT MEASURED by its own prescription (`check-test-completeness`: *"It is not a red, and there is nothing here to fix"*). ⭐ Three gates that first refused on a build prerequisite were **re-run after building the closure each named** rather than recorded as unmeasured — `check:i18n`, `check:type-check-debt`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — and all three came back green. That is the right handling of the exit-code trap: the first reading is reported as NOT MEASURED, never as a pass, and then the prerequisite is actually met. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` ran to completion, exit 0, no narrowing claimed.
